body:
hollow-test mutates source files IN PLACE. Every restore path was process-local — the runner's `finally` and a single SIGINT handler — so a run that died mid-trial stranded a live mutant as an unstaged edit. The next run then refused with `commit or stash first`, which reads as if the USER's uncommitted work is in the way; the reflex is to commit it, and that is how a mutant ships.

Observed twice: a 10-minute agent tool timeout stranded `? 130 :` flipped to `? 131 :` in a plugin CLI, and an `authorized = false` -> `true` flip was stranded the same way earlier.

## What to build

A cross-model review of the first attempt returned NO-SHIP. The scope below is the corrected one.

1. Cancellation must actually cancel. Registering a handler for a termination signal SUPPRESSES the default termination, but the trial loop was synchronous over `spawnSync`, so the handler could not be dispatched until every remaining mutant had run — measured at 24.6 seconds from SIGTERM to exit on an 8-mutant run. Trial execution therefore has to be asynchronous, cancellation has to terminate the test command's whole process group, and a cancelled run must report cancellation rather than a verdict.
2. A durable on-disk record (the file, its ORIGINAL bytes, and the MUTANT bytes) written before each mutation and consumed by the next run, which restores BEFORE the dirty-tree check. This is the only layer that survives SIGKILL, an OOM kill, or a power loss.
3. Recovery must be provable, not presumed. Restore only when the file on disk is byte-identical to the recorded mutant; anything else means the file has moved on and must not be overwritten.
4. One run at a time per worktree, enforced by an exclusive lock held across recovery, the dirty check and every trial.

The record lives in the git dir, so it is never committable and is per-worktree. A record whose owner is still alive is left alone. Probing that liveness must observe without disturbing the process.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A run cancelled by SIGTERM mid-trial stops promptly instead of running the remaining mutants, exits 143, and leaves no mutant behind.
   Verify: `node --test --test-name-pattern "SIGTERM CANCELS" packages/hollow-test/test/hollow-test.test.mjs` exits 0.
2. The same holds for SIGHUP (exit 143) and SIGINT (exit 130).
   Verify: `node --test --test-name-pattern "CANCELS the run" packages/hollow-test/test/hollow-test.test.mjs` exits 0.
3. A mutant stranded by SIGKILL is restored by the next run, reported via a `recovered` field in `--json`, instead of the dirty-tree refusal.
   Verify: `node --test --test-name-pattern "recovered by the next run" packages/hollow-test/test/hollow-test.test.mjs` exits 0.
4. A file the developer edited after the crash is NOT overwritten, and the record is kept because it holds the only copy of the original bytes.
   Verify: `node --test --test-name-pattern "refuses to overwrite work" packages/hollow-test/test/hollow-test.test.mjs` exits 0.
5. The record is written inside the git dir, is invisible to `git status`, and a run that finishes normally removes it.
   Verify: `node --test --test-name-pattern "in-flight record" packages/hollow-test/test/hollow-test.test.mjs` exits 0.
6. Ownership is tri-state: only a definite ESRCH authorises recovery; EPERM counts as alive; any other probe error is unknown and must not authorise a write. The probe uses signal 0 and never delivers a real signal.
   Verify: `node --test packages/hollow-test/test/inflight.test.mjs` exits 0.
7. A second run in the same worktree is refused while the first is alive; a lock left by a definitely-dead run is reclaimed rather than wedging the tool.
   Verify: `node --test packages/hollow-test/test/run-lock.test.mjs` exits 0.
8. Cancellation can terminate the running test command and reports honestly when there is nothing to terminate.
   Verify: `node --test packages/hollow-test/test/runner-cancel.test.mjs` exits 0.
9. The record write fails closed: if it cannot be written, the file is not mutated.
   Verify: covered by the `writeRecord THROWS` case; `node --test packages/hollow-test/test/inflight.test.mjs` exits 0.
10. No surviving mutants in the changed code.
   Verify: `node scripts/mutation-gate.mjs origin/main --max 14` exits 0.
11. No regression across the suite.
   Verify: `node scripts/run-tests.mjs` exits 0.

## Out of scope

The `adlc` dispatcher's failure to forward signals to the tool child is a separate defect with its own PR: invoked as `adlc hollow-test`, the signal never reaches this process, so even a correct handler here is unreachable. Either fix alone leaves a gap.

Rails are deliberately empty. This ticket exists to change `packages/hollow-test/`, and `rail-freeze` unions rails across every incomplete ticket — declaring a rail on the files it must edit would freeze them for every PR in the repo, including this one.
title: hollow-test must never leave a mutant in the working tree after an interrupt
